title: KV lookahead cost workshop - Optimize console walkthrough with Stratalex Analytics
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an Optimize console workshop focused on lookahead/KV prefetch and batching scenarios to reduce per-token costs for Stratalex's chat and summarization flows. Covered cost-sim spreadsheets, live Optimize recommendations, tradeoffs (latency vs unit cost), private deployment constraints (VPC, KMS), and a proposed 3-week pilot to validate savings on 2 representative endpoints.
action_items: Marisa Chen: send tailored cost-model spreadsheet + sample Optimize export by 2027-09-16
Dev Patel: provision sandbox with KV prefetch flags & 2 sample models for Stratalex by 2027-09-20
Aisha Malik: share 2 production prompt sets and 1 week of traffic heatmap by 2027-09-17
next_steps: Redwood to share cost-sim and Optimize export
Schedule 30-min kick-off for pilot week after sandbox is up
Customer to confirm pilot success criteria and SLA requirements
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 65 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Marisa Chen, Dev Patel, Laura Kim (Redwood); Aisha Malik, Tom Hargreaves, Priya Rao, Kenji Sato (Stratalex)

Summary (auto):
Quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize console for KV lookahead/prefix caching and batching cost simulations. SE demonstrated impact on token-cost per request with sample traffic shapes, and how to tune prefetch horizon and batch thresholds for Stratalex's short-chat and long-summary endpoints. Discussed private deployment KMS and RBAC concerns; customer asked about rollback and canary policies.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marisa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run a practical workshop today on lookahead and the KV prefetch knobs in Optimize, and walk through a cost sim using your typical chat and summarization flows. Dev will drive the console demo.
[00:18] Aisha Malik: sounds good, we are mainly trying to understand if we can hit a 30-40% unit cost reduction without breaching our 150ms p95 latency target for chat. Summary flows can accept higher latency up to 800ms.
[00:34] Dev Patel: great, that helps — I have a couple of traffic profiles loaded, one is chat short-turns (avg 40 tokens, bursts) and the other is doc-summarize (avg 600 tokens). We'll toggle prefetch horizon, batch windows and prefix cache TTL to show econ impact.
[00:52] Tom Hargreaves: quick note, our infra is in a VPC with strict egress rules, and we need KMS integration for any cached state stored off instance. Also team wants to know whether Dedicated nodes are required for the pilot.
[01:06] Dev Patel: good call, we'll show both hosted and dedicated sim lanes. For KMS, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM for cache encryption; in hosted we have envelope encryption but we can show key-management options.
[01:24] Priya Rao: can you explain 'lookahead' in plain terms again? We use prefix cache sometimes but not prescient lookahead.
[01:34] Dev Patel: sure — lookahead is a prefetch of the KV entries for likely next tokens based on session history and prompt templates. Instead of waiting until generation requests the KV, the runtime loads it during idle time or when session is created. This reduces token-gen latency and increases effective batching. But it costs extra memory/io and sometimes extra tokens if you prefetch unnecessary spans.
[01:56] Kenji Sato: sounds like a waste if your heuristics are wrong — what's the false-positive cost?
[02:07] Dev Patel: exactly — false prefetches add extra IO and memory but we quantify it in the sim as additional per-request I/O cost — usually shows up as a small percent of total tokens for well-formed sessions. We'll show the sim for your three heuristics: strict-match, probabilistic, and template-driven.
[02:28] Marisa Chen: I'll share the cost model later but first let's jump into the console. Dev, can you flip to the 'Optimize -> Prefetch' panel and load the chat profile?
[02:41] Dev Patel: (screen share) okay loaded 'Stratalex-chat-40t' traffic. Baseline: no prefetch, batch window 10ms, concurrency target 8, p95 latency = 132ms, token cost = $0.0012 per 1k tokens (note: transcription may garble decimals).
[03:05] Aisha Malik: that baseline p95 looks close to our threshold, nice. What's the request TPS in this sim?
[03:13] Dev Patel: sim uses 120 RPS burst windows with diurnal shape; average concurrent sessions ~320.
[03:22] (laughter, cross-talk)
[03:30] Dev Patel: now enabling prefix prefetch with a 200-token lookahead and template-driven heuristics. Also increase batching window to 30ms to allow for slightly more aggregator.
[03:46] Marisa Chen: quick reminder on the tradeoff: larger batch windows drop unit cost by improving batch sizes, but increase p95. Lookahead improves batch hit rate and reduces KV misses.
[04:02] Dev Patel: results popping in — p95 now 168ms, token cost down 28% across sim. For chat it's still under 200ms but above your 150ms target.
[04:16] Aisha Malik: hmm 168ms is borderline, our product team will push back. Is there a way to keep cost savings but bring p95 down?
[04:26] Dev Patel: yes — a hybrid: keep lookahead but reduce batch window to 18ms and use stricter heuristics (probabilistic threshold 0.7). That brings p95 to 148ms, cost saving around 22%.
[04:43] Tom Hargreaves: where does KV storage live in hosted? If we prefetch, do we persist to a shared cache across nodes?
[04:53] Dev Patel: we have both in-memory local KV caches per runtime and optional shared prefix cache backed by Redis or in-object store depending on deployment. For hosted we use a managed cache with envelope encryption. For Private, you can point to your Redis inside VPC; we support TLS and customer KMS.
[05:12] Kenji Sato: is there a consistency problem if we have many nodes?
[05:18] Dev Patel: we design for eventual consistency — lookahead is idempotent; we prefer local caches + periodic sync for hot prefixes. The Optimize console shows cache hit breakdowns.
[05:30] Aisha Malik: can you demo the cost spreadsheet and show where the 22-28% numbers come from?
[05:37] Dev Patel: sure — (switches) here's the cost-sim: rows show model compute (GPU seconds), batching multiplier, cache I/O, prefetch I/O, and effective tokens served. For chat we assume a gpt-like 7b equivalent cost baseline. I'm mapping your real RPS into tokens-per-minute.
[05:57] Marisa Chen: note: samples are conservative on compute; we'll give you the full model mapping in the spreadsheet.
[06:05] Dev Patel: for the summarization endpoint, we ran a different sim — baseline p95 620ms, token cost $0.0075 per 1k. Enabling a 1k lookahead and extended batch window to 100ms drops cost by 45% and p95 goes to 690ms which is still acceptable for your 800ms SLO.
[06:30] Priya Rao: that's promising. Any risk to output quality when you batch more aggressively? We have some deterministic prompts where ordering matters.
[06:41] Dev Patel: good question. Batching can change micro-timing but we preserve generation order and use deterministic seeds when your workload requires it. The bigger risk is KV prefix staleness in stateful chat — we recommend short TTLs (30s) and session affinity for highly stateful flows.
[07:00] Tom Hargreaves: affinity — does that mean session pinned to same runtime? We worry about node failure.
[07:09] Dev Patel: session affinity is soft; we fallback to retrieving KV from shared cache or remote store. For Dedicated we can provide sticky routing with safe failover to another pool and automatic KV warm-up.
[07:24] Aisha Malik: show me the dashboards — what metrics should we watch in the first two weeks of pilot?
[07:32] Dev Patel: Optimize's recommended dashboard: batch size distribution, cache hit ratio, p95 latency per route, extra I/O bytes per request, and token cost delta. We'll set alert thresholds for hit ratio drop >10% or p95 spike >30%.
[07:48] Marisa Chen: and we'll hook those to your slack channel if you want.
[07:52] Priya Rao: security — we need SOC 2 artifacts and proof of KMS encryption for cached data. Can you send those?
[07:59] Laura Kim: yes we'll attach SOC 2 type II and the private deployment KMS guide. Note that the hosted cache uses envelope encryption and access logs. We can generate audit logs for the pilot.
[08:12] Kenji Sato: what's the rollback mechanism if a prefetch heuristic causes regressions?
[08:18] Dev Patel: Optimize supports canary toggles per-route with automatic fallback to baseline if quality or latency thresholds are breached. We can deploy the prefetch config to 5% traffic, watch metrics for 24-48 hours, then scale.
[08:35] (brief silence)
[08:40] Marisa Chen: okay let's align on a pilot plan. Proposed: 3-week pilot, start with chat route for 1 week with canary then expand to summarize route in week two, run comparative A/B on cost and quality. Deliverables: cost-sim, sandbox with flags, success criteria doc.
[09:02] Aisha Malik: that works, we want to measure token cost delta, p95, and any quality regressions based on a small QA prompt set.
[09:12] Dev Patel: I'll include per-prompt logs for QA and a mechanism to force deterministic seeds if you want to replay.
[09:19] Tom Hargreaves: will the sandbox require Dedicated capacity? For initial test hosted is fine as long as we can replicate our VPC rules in a test environment.
[09:29] Marisa Chen: for benching, hosted sandbox is faster to start. If you require private network access we can spin a Private eval with VPC peering but that takes more lead time. We'll propose hosted sandbox by default, unless you insist on private.
[09:47] Priya Rao: we'll try hosted first, but we need KMS compatibility — can you emulate our KMS in hosted?
[09:55] Laura Kim: we can do an envelope integration and show how customer-managed keys would be used in Private. For hosted we can provide a transient key mapping for the pilot so you can validate flows.
[10:09] (longer demo showing graphs, occasional mouse noise, inaudible snippet)
[10:40] Dev Patel: one last nuance — for long tail prompts where prefetch misses are common, we recommend hybrid heuristics: only prefetch when session entropy is low or user profile indicates repeated pattern. That reduces waste.
[10:58] Kenji Sato: good, sounds like we need that for some of our rare analytics queries.
[11:06] Marisa Chen: ok wrap up — action items and next steps: we'll send the cost spreadsheet and sample Optimize export; Dev will provision the sandbox config; Aisha will share prompt sets and traffic slice. We'll get a calendar invite for pilot kickoff after sandbox provisioning.
[11:26] Aisha Malik: thanks everyone, this was really useful, appreciated the concrete numbers.
[11:31] Marisa Chen: thank you — we'll follow up by Thursday with artifacts.
[11:36] (meeting ends)
notes: Demo included live Optimize console, cost-sim spreadsheet, and configuration recommendations. Decision to pilot hosted sandbox with canary prefetch toggles. Security docs and SOC 2 to be shared. Customer emphasized 150ms chat p95 constraint.
